scoring_justification: Full recompute of eigenvalues from the agent’s parameters is infeasible due to the complexity of correctly implementing the 21×21 Γ8 Hamiltonian matrix (Eisenstein 1961) within the lightweight verifier environment. Instead we use a consistency‑based verification: parameter values are compared to the paper’s published best‑fit numbers with tolerances that absorb implementation spread, excitation energies are checked against the experimental RIXS peaks (which the agent must fit to), and the eigenvector is structurally audited for the dominant component magnitudes reported in the paper.

outputs.description: Fitted single-ion parameters, computed excitation energies, and ground-state eigenvector coefficients for Ca₃LiOsO₆. The checker will compare the fitted parameters to reference values within tolerances and verify that the ground state eigenvector has the expected dominant components.

Fitted single-ion parameters, computed excitation energies, and ground-state eigenvector coefficients for Ba₂YOsO₆. The checker will compare the fitted parameters to reference values within tolerances and verify that the ground state eigenvector has the expected dominant components.

output_contract.notes: The experimental peak energies and 10Dq values are provided as input JSON files, not hardcoded in the instruction. The checker uses hidden reference values (from the paper) to score the fitted parameters and eigenvector components.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference parameter values, tolerances, gold excitation energies, and eigenvector magnitude ranges for each compound.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper’s main text and supplementary material (arXiv:1610.02375).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Transcribed directly from the paper’s reported best‑fit values and experimental peak energies.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper’s own published numbers used as the hidden gold for reproduced parameters and energies.
